scope: Existing borrowed HF technical and target-runtime evidence only; original facts, source-level review dates and conflicts are unchanged.

sections: Key points for upgrading to version 10.0
Support for version 3.7 of the Python runtime environment has been removed
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 22 bounded semantic recheck: Python 3.9 is the 10.0 default, Python 3.7 support is removed, and apps and add-ons must be compatible with 3.9. This does not establish UF applicability, compatibility for every installed or app-owned runtime, or a deployment approval.

sections: Key points for upgrading to version 10.0 — FIPS-mode module requirements and dedicated migration link
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 21 bounded semantic recheck: the 10.0 source introduces a FIPS 140-3-compliant module only for FIPS-mode instances and sends those deployments to a dedicated prerequisite and migration procedure. This is not a transparent switch, a UF rule, FedRAMP authorization or a claim that every HF runs in FIPS mode.

sections: Key points for upgrading to version 10.0 — SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 deprecation
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 21 bounded semantic recheck: SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 remain supported in 10.0 with warnings while deprecated; the source recommends TLS 1.2 or higher and anticipates certificate work. This is not 10.4 removal, a UF requirement or a deployment approval.

sections: Splunk Enterprise no longer lets you run it as the root user by default
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 22 bounded semantic recheck: Splunk Enterprise 10.2 blocks root execution by default on Unix-like systems, permits the temporary --run-as-root override, and recommends a least-privileged non-root account. This does not establish UF applicability, every installed app's identity requirements, or deployment approval.

sections: The Splunk Fishbucket database back end has been replaced
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 22 bounded semantic recheck: the replacement backend reads legacy checkpoints and writes new checkpoints without an explicit or implicit migration. An unsupported downgrade can miss newer checkpoints and cause reingestion or duplicate data. This does not establish UF applicability, checkpoint loss during a supported upgrade, or a supported rollback path.

sections: Upgrade Splunk Python version from 3.9 to 3.13
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. This does not establish UF applicability, compatibility for every installed or app-owned runtime, or deployment approval.

sections: Splunk has removed support for versions 1.0 and 1.1 of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 24 semantic recheck: READ THIS FIRST says TLS 1.0/1.1 support was completely removed in 10.4, while the current TLS guide says both are off by default and can be temporarily re-enabled with deprecatedTlsVersionSupport. Preserve the conflict. This is not a UF rule, Cloud-managed installation requirement, or deployment approval.

sections: Prepare for upgrade
Optional: Postpone the automatic database upgrade to a cohosted KV store before it begins
claims.qualification: Applies only to an Enterprise-package HF with KV Store. October 25 bounded semantic recheck: the current guide requires KV Store 7.0+, more than 50% free disk space, health checks and a parallel backup; migration starts automatically unless postponed, impairs writes, and requires ITSI 5.0.x and lower to postpone with postgresMigrateOnStartup=false verified on every member. ES incompatibility remains separately cited to the matrix; omission here is not clearance. No UF applicability, pairing, entitlement or authorization is inferred.
